provider: DedicatedCore — 6 TB storage VPS, 60 days free (3 slots only)

free_tier.stated: 6 TB HDD, 3 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 10,000 GB bandwidth, dedicated IP — free for 60 days. Only 3 units existed.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: until the instance is recycled; not persistent

egress.terms: 10 TB/month included; not unmetered, not CF-covered. At a 500 GB–1 TiB/day serving rate this is ~10-20 days of traffic.

tooling: Root KVM — SSH/SFTP/rsync, so rclone sftp or a local fuse mount works. No object API.
chaining: Not repeatable. Explicitly 'non-renewable, and the VPS will be deleted at the end of the 60-day period', 3 slots, application via a Google Form, and the thread closed with 'Filled!' within days. This is a marketing gesture, not a capacity source.
limits_note: 60 days hard delete. Terms restrict it to 'storage or backup purposes only' — no websites, no streaming, no high-traffic services, so the serving workload is excluded by contract from the start.
reliability_note: Deliberately ephemeral: the data is destroyed at day 60 by design. Good for one 6 TB cold-archive burst, worthless as standing storage.
confidence_note: mechanically converted from the seed corpus; no page was read for this record in the storage-dossier pass. One page read moves it to documented.
